q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a saree?
title: Saree carbon footprint per saree
short: Start with the fabric: yarn per saree including border and pallu, then weaving power. Add dyeing, printing or zari work and finishing steam, divide the unit's energy by sarees finished, and state the fibre, length and weight.
audience: Saree weavers, processors and sellers in Surat, Varanasi and Kanchipuram

ul: Yarn by fibre and weight: silk, cotton, polyester or viscose.
Zari or metallic thread by weight.
Power loom electricity, or handloom with no machine energy.
Dyeing or printing: dye, chemicals and steam per metre.

p: Report per saree with its fibre, length and weight. A heavy silk saree with zari and a light printed polyester saree are very different products.

example.title: Worked example: saree unit per saree (one month)
lines: Plant total: 19,325 / 10,000 = 1.933 kg CO2 per saree
Add yarn, zari and dyes for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
